title: Which MacBook Should You Buy in 2026?
summary: Apple's 2026 lineup has three clear tiers: the budget MacBook Neo, the mainstream MacBook Air and the high-performance MacBook Pro.
method: Picks come from Macworld and Tom's Guide buying guides, cross-checked with Envirofone and Refurbed comparisons. Only models covered by at least two of these sources are listed.
assumptions: Apple raised MacBook prices in 2026 (Macworld reports a $200 rise on the Air in June), so we show no prices here. Check the current price before you buy.

products.name: Apple MacBook Air 13-inch (M5, 2026)
why: Macworld names the 13-inch M5 Air the best MacBook overall and Tom's Guide calls it a fantastic laptop for most people. The M5 Air arrived in March 2026.
Tom's Guide reports battery life of over 15 hours, and Macworld notes it can drive two external displays.
specs: Memory and storage cannot be upgraded later
cons: RAM and storage are fixed, so buy the size you need up front
products.best_for: Students, professionals and anyone who wants one MacBook for everything
products.skip_if: You need sustained heavy workloads or the Pro's better display

products.name: Apple MacBook Neo
why: Macworld calls the MacBook Neo the cheapest way to buy a Mac laptop in 2026, and Tom's Guide calls it an exemplary budget laptop for the price.
It uses the A18 Pro chip. Refurbed says the M5 in the Air has roughly double its multi-core and GPU performance, so it suits lighter use.
specs: About half the multi-core and GPU speed of the M5 Air (Refurbed)
cons: Less powerful than the Air and Pro
products.best_for: Budget buyers with light needs: browsing, schoolwork, email
products.skip_if: You edit video, code heavily or want the long-term headroom of the Air

products.name: Apple MacBook Pro 14-inch (M5)
why: Tom's Guide names the 14-inch M5 the best MacBook Pro overall: strong performance, long battery life and easy to carry.
Macworld recommends it for people who need sustained performance and better displays than the Air offers. Tom's Guide notes it is not a huge upgrade over the M4 model.
specs: Not a big jump from the M4 Pro-class model (Tom's Guide)
cons: Costs much more than the Air
products.best_for: Power users who want a dependable Pro that travels well
products.skip_if: Your work is light enough for the Air, or you need maximum GPU power

products.name: Apple MacBook Pro (M5 Pro / M5 Max)
why: Macworld points creative pros, developers and high-end video editors to the M5 Pro and M5 Max Pros. Tom's Guide picks the M5 Pro for its strong GPU for video edits and AI work.
Refurbed names the 14-inch M5 Pro with 64 GB of memory the best configuration for photo and video creators.
specs: M5 Pro or M5 Max chip
Envirofone puts the 14-inch M5 at about £1,599 new, with M5 Pro/Max climbing past £3,000 (UK prices)
products.best_for: Video editors, developers and creative professionals
products.skip_if: You mostly browse, write and stream
